titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §201: Jamuqa's last words
about: The end of Jamuqa, Chinggis's sworn friend turned rival. Jamuqa, taken at last, makes a long speech recalling their pledge as boys and asking for death without bloodshed and burial on high ground; Chinggis answers with an account of Jamuqa's faults and grants the request.

sentences.t: ügüleġesü Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Speaking-if, Žamuqa, saying:
sentences.i: When he had spoken, Jamuqa said:
sentences.n: A turn-taking formula: ügüle- 'to speak' appears twice, first as a conditional converb (-ġesü, 'if, when') and then as a converb (-rün, 'on saying'). The conditional has no stated subject; I take it to be the previous speaker, Chinggis, so 'when he had spoken' is an inference, not something the words say.

sentences.t: "Erte üdür üčüged čaγ-tur Qorqonaγ-Žubur-a Qān anda- luγ̇a anda keġeldürün
sentences.l: Early days, small-ones time-at, at Qorqonaγ-Žubur, Qān anda-with, anda saying-to-each-other-when,
sentences.i: “In the early days, when we were small, at Qorqonaq-Jubur, when the Qan and I called each other anda,
sentences.n: Shiratori opens Jamuqa's speech at Erte (the quotation mark is his); it runs to ötörletüġei, where he closes it. Qān here is the Ming 皇帝 and means Chinggis, spelled Qān rather than Qaγan; `i` writes Qān as 'Qan' and Qaγan as 'Qahan', as in §200. anda is the sworn friend, a bond closer than friendship (rendered 'sworn brother' elsewhere in `i`; here the word itself is what they call each other); the edition cuts anda-luγ̇a at the line end, 'with the anda'; keġeldürün is keġe- 'say' + -ldü- 'to each other' + -rün 'when'. üčüged is üčüge 'small' with the plural -d (Ming 每).

morph.gloss: sworn friend, oath-brother (the hyphen joins it to luγ̇a) [契合]
comitative: with, together with (case suffix; the hyphen after anda- is the printer's, at the line end) [一同]

sentences.t: ülü šiṅgeküi ideġe ideldüžü ülü umartaqu üges ügüleldüžü
sentences.l: Not digesting food, eating-together; not forgettable words, speaking-together,
sentences.i: we ate together food that would not digest, and spoke together words not to be forgotten,
sentences.n: ülü is the negative that stands before participles (ese, by contrast, negates past verbs): ülü šiṅgeküi, ülü umartaqu. The -ldü- in ideldüžü and ügüleldüžü means 'together'; -žü is the converb that chains the clauses. 'Food that does not digest' is the Ming 消化的 read literally; I take it as an oath-idiom for a bond that lasts, but that is my reading, not the glossators'.

morph.gloss: to be absorbed, sink in (digest; set, of the sun) [消化的]

sentences.t: künžile-deġen qaγaldažu aγdažuγ̇u-že.
sentences.l: Blanket-in-our-own sharing, covered we were, indeed.
sentences.i: we shared our blanket and lay covered.
sentences.n: -deġen is a reflexive possessive on a dative-locative stem (Ming 自的行, 'one's own'). The pair qaγaldažu / aγdažuγ̇u is uncertain: the Ming give 分着 'dividing' and 被住着 'being covered', and I join them as sharing the blanket. -že is the emphatic sentence particle (Ming 也者).

morph.gloss: dative-locative with reflexive possessive: 'in/among one's own' [自的行]
to share out, divide (stem uncertain; Ming 分) [分着]
to be covered, lie covered (Ming 被住) [被住着有來 也者︀]

sentences.t: Köndöledü-de kökiġüldežü γalžirqu-da qadquγdažu qaγačan baražu
sentences.l: By bystanders incited, by the crooked one struck-down, parting, finishing,
sentences.i: Egged on by bystanders, struck at by crooked men, we parted and were done with each other;
sentences.n: A passive with an agent: qadquγdažu carries the passive -γda-; kökiġüldežü I take as passive too, though its -lde- is my guess and the Ming 挑唆着 is plain 'inciting'. The doer takes the dative-locative -de/-da, which the Ming render with 被 … 行, 'suffering at the hands of'. Köndöledü (傍人, 'people at the side') and γalžirqu (斜人, 'slanting person') are both uncertain in form; qaγačan baražu is 'parted and finished'.

morph.gloss: side, one at the side, bystander (form köndöledü uncertain; Ming 傍人) [被傍人行]
dative-locative, 'by' the agent of a passive [行]
to be incited, be egged on [挑唆着]
to be slanting, crooked (Ming 斜) [被斜人 行]
to strike, stab, slay (Ming 戮) [戮着]

sentences.t: qadaγatu üges üġüleldüleġe keġen
sentences.l: Weighty words speaking-together, saying:
sentences.i: saying, ‘We have spoken weighty words together,’
sentences.n: keġen (keġe- 'say' + -n) closes a quotation or a thought. qadaγatu is 'having weight' (Ming 緊要有的); I read the whole as what the two men said to one another in pledging themselves. The sentence does not close here; the next two units finish the thought.

morph.gloss: weight, pressing importance (Ming 緊要) [緊要 有的]

sentences.t: qara niγ̇ur(i)-jan qaγ̇uldaqui-ača qalidun jadan
sentences.l: Black face-own flayed-from, close unable,
sentences.i: for fear my black face would be flayed, I could not come near;
sentences.n: niγ̇ur(i)-jan is 'face' with the reflexive possessive, 'my own face'; -ača is the ablative (Ming 行), 'from, because of'. Being 'flayed' (Ming 被剝) is surely shame, but whether the clause means 'because of' or 'rather than' is not certain, so 'for fear' is mine. jadan is jada- 'be unable' as a converb.

morph.gloss: face (Ming 面皮) [面皮 自的行]
reflexive possessive 'my own', here after an -i linking vowel [自的行]
to be flayed, peeled (Ming 被剝) [被剝的 行]

sentences.t: Qān anda-ijan qalaγ̇un čirai üžen jadažu jabuba-že bi.
sentences.l: Qān my-own-anda’s warm face seeing unable, went I.
sentences.i: I could not look on the warm face of my sworn brother the Qan, and I went away.
sentences.n: anda-ijan puts the reflexive possessive on anda: 'my own anda'. jadažu with a converb of seeing is 'unable to see'; jabuba-že is jabu- 'go' in the past with the particle -že. This is the first of a matched pair of sentences, one with a black face, one with a red.

morph.gloss: to go, walk [行了 也者︀]

sentences.t: Ülü umartaqu üges üġüleldüleġe keġen
sentences.l: Not forgettable words speaking-together, saying:
sentences.i: saying, ‘We have spoken words not to be forgotten,’
sentences.n: The pair to the earlier 'weighty words' line: ülü umartaqu üges, 'words not to be forgotten', again closed by keġen.

sentences.t: hulaγ̇an niγ̇ur(i)-jan übčigdeküi-eče
sentences.l: Red face-own flayed-from,
sentences.i: and for fear my red face would be flayed,
sentences.n: hulaγ̇an niγ̇ur(i)-jan answers qara niγ̇ur(i)-jan above; übčigdeküi has the same structure as qaγ̇uldaqui (passive + participle + ablative). 'For fear' is mine here as in the earlier clause. Why the face is black in one clause and red in the other the text does not say; I leave both colours and do not explain them. The clause is left open, completed in the next unit.

morph.gloss: face (Ming 面皮) [面皮 自的行]
reflexive possessive 'my own', here after an -i linking vowel [自的行]
to peel, flay (Ming 被剝) [被剝的 行]

sentences.t: urtu sedkiltü anda-ijan ünen čirai üžen jadažu jabuba-že bi.
sentences.l: Long-hearted anda-own true face seeing unable, went I.
sentences.i: I could not look on the true face of my long-hearted sworn brother, and I went away.
sentences.n: urtu sedkiltü is 'long-hearted' (Ming 長 / 心有的), an epithet of anda, not of the face; I take it as steadfast, enduring, but the Ming give only the parts. The grammar repeats the earlier jadažu jabuba-že bi.

morph.gloss: to go, walk [行了 也者︀]

sentences.t: Edöġe Qān anda min-u sojurγažu nama-ji nököčeje keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Now Qān anda my, favouring, me-(object) ‘let us be companions’ has said.
sentences.i: Now the Qan, my sworn brother, in his grace has said to me, ‘Let us be companions.’
sentences.n: nama-ji is bi 'I': the oblique stem nama- with the accusative -ji; the Ming gloss it 我行, 'to me'. nököčeje is nököče- 'be a companion' with the hortative -je (Ming 咱, 'let us'). keġežüġüi is keġe- 'say' with the past ending -žüġüi, the front-vowel form of -žuγ̇ui (Ming 說了有).

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow grace [恩賜 着]

sentences.t: Nököčeküi čaγ-tur ese nököčeldübe bi.
sentences.l: Companion-being time-at, not companion-became I.
sentences.i: But at the time for being a companion I did not become one.
sentences.n: Nököčeküi čaγ-tur is a participle before 'time', 'at the time of being a companion'. ese before a past verb is 'did not'. The 'But' is mine: nothing in the Mongolian joins the two ideas except contrast.

morph.gloss: not (negative of the past tense) [不曾]

sentences.t: Edöġe anda toγoriγai ulus-i tübšidgebe.
sentences.l: Now anda round realm-(object) pacified.
sentences.i: Now, sworn brother, you have brought peace to the realm all around,
sentences.n: toγoriγai (Ming 圓, 'round') is uncertain in form; I take it as 'all around'. tübšidgebe is the past of a causative, 'made peaceful' (Ming 敎平了). -i on ulus marks the object (Ming 行). 'You' and the address 'sworn brother' are my reading: the verb carries no person.

morph.gloss: round, all around, in a circle (Ming 圓; form uncertain) [圓]
to pacify, bring to peace [敎平了]

sentences.t: Qari tutum-i qamtudγaba
sentences.l: Foreign each-(object) united.
sentences.i: and united every foreign people.
sentences.n: qari is 'foreign' (外邦). tutum is 'each, every one' in the glossary; the Ming write 每行, 'each', and the -i makes it the object, so 'every foreign one'; 'people' is my filling of the noun. qamtudγaba is 'joined together'.

sentences.t: či Qān oro čima-dur žoriba.
sentences.l: You Qān throne, to-you pointed.
sentences.i: The Qan’s throne has been marked out for you.
sentences.n: Qān oro is a noun before a noun, 'Qan throne' (Ming 皇帝 位(子)), hence 'the Qan's throne'; či 'you' is then repeated in čima-dur, which I do not render twice. The doer is not stated: žoriba is 'pointed out, designated' and the Ming gloss simply 指了, so I leave it passive. čima-dur is či 'you' in its dative-locative stem.

morph.gloss: to aim, point out, destine [指了]

sentences.t: Delegei edöġe belen boluγsan-dur nököčežü jaγ̇un tusa bolqu bi.
sentences.l: The world now ready when-it-has-become, companion-being, what use being I?
sentences.i: Now that the world lies ready, what use would I be as a companion?
sentences.n: boluγsan-dur is 'when it has become' (participle + dative-locative, Ming 時). jaγ̇un tusa bolqu bi is a question without a question word of its own beyond jaγ̇un 'what': 'what service shall I be'. Delegei is capitalised because it opens a sentence (žoriba. closes the one before).

sentences.t: Munda anda-jin qara šünin-ü žeġüdün-dür čin-u oroqu bi.
sentences.l: But, anda’s, black night’s dream-in, yours entering I.
sentences.i: But into your dreams on the black night, sworn brother, I shall enter;
sentences.n: Munda is Ming 卻, 'on the contrary, but'. anda-jin is a genitive ('of the anda', Ming 契合 的); I read it as the address 'sworn brother' because čin-u 'your' follows and both cannot be possessors of the dream, but that is uncertain. The object of oroqu is left open: čin-u 'yours' leaves a noun to supply, and 'your dreams' (the dream already named) is my reading.

morph.gloss: on the contrary, rather; the Ming read it as a conjunction, 'but' [卻]

sentences.t: Gegeġen üdür-ün sedkil čin-u žubaγ̇aqu bi.
sentences.l: Bright day’s your heart troubling I.
sentences.i: by bright day I shall trouble your heart;
sentences.n: žubaγ̇aqu is glossed 敎生受, 'to cause hardship'. The pair with the dream line is plain parallelism, night and day: he will not let go of him in either.

morph.gloss: to trouble, cause distress (Ming 敎生受) [敎生受]

sentences.t: Žaqa-jin čin-u böġešün žagiṅ-ün čin-u örügešün bolqu bi.
sentences.l: Collar’s your vermin, hem’s your thorn becoming I.
sentences.i: I shall be a pest in your collar and a thorn in your hem.
sentences.n: Two paired figures, both genitives ending with čin-u 'your'. böġešün is Ming 蟲子 'insect, vermin', perhaps a louse; žagiṅ is 底襟, the under-flap of a robe; örügešün is 刺 'thorn'. The sense, a nuisance he will always be, is plain even where the nouns are not.

morph.gloss: vermin, crawling pest (Ming 蟲子; perhaps a louse) [䖝子]
lower hem, under-flap of a coat (Ming 底襟) [底襟 的]

sentences.t: Arbin emegetü büleġe bi.
sentences.l: Broad grandmother-having was I.
sentences.i: I was one who had a broad old woman.
sentences.n: This line I cannot recover. The Ming give 寬廣 'wide' and 婆婆有的 'having a grandmother', and the English follows them literally; I take it to be an idiom of self-reproach, but I do not know what it idiomatically says. -tü is the possessive, 'having'.

morph.gloss: old woman, grandmother [婆婆 有的]

sentences.t: Anda-ača alus-i sedkikü bolun alžiγ̇as boldaba bi.
sentences.l: Anda-from beyond thinking, being, error became I.
sentences.i: Thinking to hold myself apart from my sworn brother, I fell into error.
sentences.n: alus-i is 'beyond(?)' in house usage (Ming 隔越, 'cross over, be separated'); 'hold myself apart' is my reading of alus-i with anda-ača, 'from the anda'. sedkikü bolun is a participle with a converb of bol-, 'being thinking of'; boldaba is a passive past, Ming 被做了.

morph.gloss: beyond, across (uncertain; Ming 隔越 'to separate, pass over') [隔越(行)]
error, mistake, going astray (Ming 差) [差]

sentences.t: Edöġe ene törelki-dür anda ba qojar-un urγuqui naran-(n)ača šiṅgeküi naran-dur kürtele nere min-u kürbe-že.
sentences.l: Now this birth-in, anda, we two’s rising sun-from, setting sun-at until, name my reached.
sentences.i: Now, in this life, sworn brother, my name, the name of the two of us, has reached from where the sun rises to where it sets.
sentences.n: Read this as a unit of two limits: naran-(n)ača … naran-dur … kürtele, 'from sun … to sun'. šiṅgeküi, which meant 'digest' earlier, here means 'set' (Ming 落的): šiṅge- 'sink in'. How ba qojar-un 'of the two of us' hangs on nere min-u 'my name' is my reading, not certain.

morph.gloss: we (first-person plural pronoun; Ming 俺) [俺]
to be absorbed, sink in (digest; set, of the sun) [落的]

sentences.t: Anda sečen eketü törülki külüg törežü erdemten
sentences.l: Anda, wise mother-having, birth-nature, hero born, skill-having-ones,
sentences.i: My sworn brother, with a wise mother, born to his nature, born a hero, with men of skill,
sentences.n: A chain of descriptions of anda (Chinggis), Jamuqa's rival, not yet joined to a verb. -tü is the possessive 'having'; törülki is 'inborn nature' (Ming 生的), a word I meet again below; erdemten is erdem 'skill' + -ten, the plural of -tü, 'those having skill', so it names followers and belongs with the companions of the next unit rather than with anda himself.

morph.gloss: nature of one's birth, inborn quality (Ming 生的) [生的]

sentences.t: deġü-nertü orluγ̇ud nököd(i)-dür(i)-jen dalan γurban aγtas(i)-jar(i)-jan bolžu anda-da hülegdebe-že.
sentences.l: Younger-brothers-having, mighty ones companions-own-to, seventy three geldings-own-with, being, anda-by was overcome.
sentences.i: with brothers, with mighty men for his own companions, with seventy-three geldings of his own: by such a sworn brother I was overcome.
sentences.n: A long chain broken here (deġü-nertü is deġü-ner 'younger brothers' + -tü 'having', Ming 兄弟每有的; the contrast is with Jamuqa's own deġü-ner ügeiġü below); bolžu 'being' carries it, with anda the subject, and the passive hülegdebe-že 'was overcome' ends it, with anda-da as the agent (Ming 行). -dür(i)-jen and -jar(i)-jan are case endings with the reflexive possessive: 'among his own companions', 'with his own geldings'. The Ming say 'geldings' (騸馬); whether that is literal or a figure for men I cannot tell.

morph.gloss: instrumental: 'with' (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel) [自的行]
dative-locative, 'by' the agent of a passive [行]
to overcome, surpass (Ming 勝) [被 勝 了也者︀]

sentences.t: Bi bürün eke ečige-dēče üčügen qočorču deġü-ner ügeiġü,
sentences.l: I being, mother father-from small left-behind, younger-brothers none,
sentences.i: I, left behind from my mother and father while small, have no younger brothers,
sentences.n: bürün is bü- 'be' + the converb of time -rün (Ming 有的); after bi I take it as 'as for me', but that is uncertain. ečige-dēče is the ablative with a long vowel, as printed. ügeiġü is ügei 'without' with an extra -ġü.

morph.gloss: without, there is not (here with an added -ġü) [無]

sentences.t: eme min-u domoγži itegel ügeiġü
sentences.l: Wife my talker, reliance none,
sentences.i: my wife is a talker, and there is nothing to lean on;
sentences.n: domoγži is domoγ 'tale, talk' with the agent suffix -ži (Ming 好長話, 'good long speech'); whether it is praise or complaint the Mongolian leaves open. itegel ügeiġü is 'there is no reliance'.

morph.gloss: agent suffix 'one who tells' (Ming 好長話)
without, there is not (here with an added -ġü) [無]

sentences.t: nöködtü teġü-ber teṅgeri-eče žajaγ̇atu anda-da hülegdebe-že.
sentences.l: Companions-having, that-by, Heaven-from destiny-having, anda-by was overcome.
sentences.i: I have companions, and for that reason I have been overcome by my sworn brother, who has a destiny from Heaven.
sentences.n: The subject of nöködtü 'having companions' is not marked; I take it to be Jamuqa himself, who has just listed what he lacks; the sense seems to be that companions are all he has, but 'only' is not in the text. teġü-ber 'by that' is 'therefore'. žajaγ̇atu is 'fate-having' (Ming 命有的), the epithet of a man chosen by Heaven.

morph.gloss: that; teġü- is its stem before a case ending [爲那般]
dative-locative, 'by' the agent of a passive [行]
to overcome, surpass (Ming 勝) [被 勝 了也者︀]

sentences.t: Anda sojurγaγ̇asu nama-ji ötör nögčeġesü
sentences.l: Anda, graciously-if, me-(object) quickly pass-away-if,
sentences.i: Sworn brother, if you would be gracious and let me pass quickly,
sentences.n: Two conditionals in -γ̇asu / -ġesü (Ming 呵). nögče- is 'to pass on' (Ming 過去, the euphemism for dying), here 'let me pass quickly'; the Ming 敎 'cause' shows no causative suffix in the form (compare nögčiġe- below). The verb of the main clause comes in the next line.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow grace [恩賜呵]
to pass away, cause to pass on (Ming 敎過去) [敎過去呵]

sentences.t: anda žürüge-ben amumu-že či.
sentences.l: Anda, heart-own at ease, you.
sentences.i: your heart, sworn brother, will be at ease.
sentences.n: -ben is the reflexive possessive 'one's own', here on 'heart'. amumu-že is amu- 'rest, be at peace' in the present with the emphatic -že; 'will be' is my reading of a present tense that states a result.

morph.gloss: to be at peace, rest [安有也者︀]

sentences.t: Anda sojurγažu alaγ̇ulurun čisu ülü γarγan alaγ̇ul.
sentences.l: Anda, graciously, causing-to-kill-when, blood not bringing-out, cause-to-kill.
sentences.i: Sworn brother, when in your grace you have me killed, have me killed without bringing out my blood.
sentences.n: alaγ̇ul- is ala- 'kill' with the causative -γ̇ul-, 'have killed'; γarγan is the causative of γar- 'come out' with -n, 'making come out'. The request that no blood be shed is the crux of what follows in the next scene, where Chinggis grants it.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow grace [恩賜着]

sentences.t: Üküžü kebteġesü ölüg jasun min-u ündür etügen-dür
sentences.l: Dying, if (I) lie-down, dead bone my, high earth-on,
sentences.i: If I die and lie down, my dead bones, on high ground,
sentences.n: etügen is 'earth' (Ming 地), here the plain word, 'ground'. ündür etügen-dür is 'on high ground'. kebteġesü is kebte- 'to lie' as a conditional.

sentences.t: eġüre tuluγ uruγ-un uruγ-a čin-u kürtele igežü ögsü;
sentences.l: Long, far, descendants-of descendants-to, yours until, protecting, give-let;
sentences.i: for long and far, down to your descendants’ descendants, may I give protection and help;
sentences.n: eġüre tuluγ is a doublet, 'long and far' (Ming 久 遠). uruγ-un uruγ-a is 'to the descendants of descendants', the genitive and the dative-locative on the same noun. igežü ögsü, 'protecting, may I give', is Ming 護助着 與; the subject of ögsü is not marked, and I take it as the speaker's bones, so 'I'.

morph.gloss: to help, protect (Ming 護助) [護助着]

sentences.t: hirüġer boluju-že bi.
sentences.l: Blessing becoming I.
sentences.i: I shall be a blessing.
sentences.n: hirüġer, Ming 祝壽 'to wish long life', is a blessing or prayer. boluju-že bi: bol- 'be' with the present ending -ju (as in the glossary's boluju) and -že; the present tense reads as a promise here, hence 'shall be'.

morph.gloss: blessing, prayer for long life (Ming 祝壽) [祝︀壽]
to be, become [做有 也者︀]

sentences.t: Hužaγ̇ur öġere törülkitü büleġe bi.
sentences.l: Origin different, natured was I.
sentences.i: In my origin I was of a different nature;
sentences.n: hužaγ̇ur is 'root' (as in the opening lines of the book); öġere is 'different'; törülkitü is törülki 'inborn nature' + the possessive -tü. büleġe is bü- 'be' in the past.

sentences.t: Hüleġü törülkitü anda-jin sülder-e daruγdaba-že bi.
sentences.l: Surplus-natured anda’s might-by was-pressed I.
sentences.i: and I was crushed by the might of my sworn brother, who was of greater nature.
sentences.n: Hüleġü is 'surplus, more' (Ming 多餘) and modifies anda's nature. daruγdaba-že is the passive of daru- 'press down', with the particle -že. sülder-e (威靈) is 'might' with the dative-locative that the Ming read as agent, 'by'.

morph.gloss: surplus, excess, greater (Ming 多餘) [多餘]
to press down, overpower [被壓了也者︀]

sentences.t: Ügülegsen üges min-u ülü umartan üde manaγar duradču ügüleldüdkün ta.
sentences.l: Spoken words my not forgetting, evening, morning remembering, speak-together, you all.
sentences.i: Not forgetting the words I have spoken, and remembering them evening and morning, speak of them together, all of you.
sentences.n: The plural imperative -dkün (Ming 您) addresses the listeners; ta is 'you all'. umartan is 'forgetting' as a converb with ülü 'not'. duradču is dura- 'remember' with the converb -dču (the glossary's reading; the d is unexplained). ülü umartan and duradču are converbs leading to the imperative ügüleldüdkün. üde and manaγar are 'evening' and 'morning'.

morph.gloss: to remember, think of (the d of -dču is unexplained, as in the glossary) [想着]

sentences.t: Edöġe nama-ji ötörletüġei" keġen ügüleġesü
sentences.l: Now me hasten-let, saying, speaking-if.
sentences.i: Now let it be quick for me,” he said. When he had spoken,
sentences.n: Shiratori closes the quotation here (ötörletüġei"). ötörle- is 'to hurry' (ötör 'quick') with the imperative -tüġei, 'let them hasten'; what is hastened, his death, is left unsaid. ügüleġesü returns to the turn-taking formula of the opening, here 'when he had spoken'.

morph.gloss: to hurry, be swift (ötör 'quick') [敎疾快者︀]

sentences.t: edeġer üges-tür in-ü Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: These words-in, his, Čiṅgis Qaγan, saying:
sentences.i: At these words of his Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: edeġer is 'these' (Ming 這每), a plural form beside ede. in-ü is the genitive of the third person, 'his', and Middle Mongol sets it after the noun it belongs to; here it points back to Jamuqa. The Ming bracket 太祖 over Čiṅgis, a Chinese title for the founder.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖]

sentences.t: "Anda min-u aṅgida ber jabužu
sentences.l: Anda my outside too, going,
sentences.i: “Even when my sworn brother went apart from us,
sentences.n: Chinggis's speech opens here (Shiratori's quotation mark is on Anda) and runs to ügüle". aṅgida is Ming 外 'outside, apart'; ber is 'also, even'. The two units that follow are a converb chain I have cut in two.

sentences.t: bidan-dur aman düġüren keleležü amin-dur qor sedkikü-ji in-ü ese sonosdaba-že.
sentences.l: Us-to mouth full speaking, life-to harm thinking-the his not (we) heard.
sentences.i: though he spoke to us with a full mouth, we never heard of his thought of harm to life.
sentences.n: aman düġüren keleležü, 'speaking with a full mouth', is the Ming 口滿說着; I take it as 'at length, in earnest'. sedkikü-ji marks 'the thinking' as object; ese … sonosdaba-že is 'was not heard' (Ming 不曾聽的了); -da- may be passive or middle, so 'we never heard of' is safer than 'we paid no heed'. Whose life, and who thought the harm, is not stated; the reading above is mine.

morph.gloss: to speak, to say (kele 'tongue, language') [說着]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
not (negative of the past tense) [不曾]

sentences.t: Surdaqu küġün büleġe.
sentences.l: Learnable man was.
sentences.i: He was a man one could learn from.
sentences.n: Surdaqu (Ming 可學的, 'learnable') has two possible senses: 'worth learning from' or 'able to learn'. I take the first. büleġe is bü- 'be' in the past.

morph.gloss: to be learned from (sur- 'learn' + -da-; Ming 可學) [可學的]

sentences.t: Mün ülü bolumui; üküġülüje kēġesü tölge-dür ülü oromui.
sentences.l: Only not willing is; cause-to-die-let-us if (one) says, omen-in not entering is.
sentences.i: It is simply not agreeable; if one says, ‘Let us put him to death,’ it does not come into the omen.
sentences.n: mün (Ming 只) is 'only, simply'. bolumui is bol- + -umui with the Ming 肯有, 'is willing, agreeable'. tölge (卦) is a divination or omen, and 'does not enter the omen' is Ming 不入卦裏: such a killing would not be sanctioned by the signs. Both clauses have no stated subject.

morph.gloss: to become, be; here 'to be willing, agreeable' (Ming 肯) [肯有]

sentences.t: Siltaγ̇an ügei amin-dur qor kiġešü ülü žokimui.
sentences.l: Cause without, life-to harm if (one) does, not fitting.
sentences.i: If one does harm to a life without cause, it is not fitting.
sentences.n: siltaγ̇an ügei is 'without reason'. kiġešü is the conditional of ki- 'do', Ming 做呵. žokimui is žoki- 'be fitting' in the present: it states a rule, not a single act.

sentences.t: Kündü mörtü küġün bi.
sentences.l: Weighty path-having person there-is.
sentences.i: There is a man of weighty ways.
sentences.n: This bi is the verb 'is, there is' (Ming 有), not the pronoun 'I' that appears elsewhere. kündü mörtü, 'weighty-path-having' (Ming 重 道子有的), may mean a man of rank or dignity; who is meant is not stated, and 'a man of weighty ways' is what the glosses give.

morph.gloss: there is (existential bi, not the pronoun 'I') [有]

sentences.t: Ene maqa siltaγ̇an in-ü ügüledkün.
sentences.l: This perhaps cause his; speak (pl.).
sentences.i: Perhaps this is his reason; say so.
sentences.n: maqa is 'perhaps (not)' in house usage. The imperative -dkün is plural, so Chinggis is speaking to the men about him and charging them with a message. in-ü is 'his'. I read this as a hinge to what follows: the cause Chinggis then gives.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Erte Sožidar-Mala, Taičar qojar-un aduγ̇u-ban deġermedülčegsen-ü tula
sentences.l: Formerly Sožidar-Mala, Taičar two’s herds-own mutually-plundering-of on-account,
sentences.i: Because in former days Sojidar-Mala and Taichar plundered one another’s herds,
sentences.n: From here to keġen ügüledkün (unit 51) runs the message Chinggis tells his men to carry to Jamuqa; Shiratori marks it with no quotation marks and I add none. A reciprocal: deġermedülče- (Ming 共劫了, 'plundered together') with -ldü- 'each other' is how I read the form; the stem is not certain. aduγ̇u-ban is 'their own herd'. tula 'on account of' follows a genitive. The two names are Shiratori's spellings; my English forms are by the house rules.

morph.gloss: to plunder one another (Ming 共劫; stem uncertain) [共劫了的]
on account of, because of (postposition after a genitive) [上頭]

sentences.t: Žamuqa anda či buruγ̇uj-a bulγa qoidčü irežü
sentences.l: Žamuqa anda, you, on-purpose rebellion plotting, coming,
sentences.i: you, Jamuqa, my sworn brother, deliberately plotted rebellion and came,
sentences.n: buruγ̇uj-a (Ming 特地行, 'on purpose') is an adverb whose stem I cannot fix. qoidčü (Ming 謀起着, 'plotting') is likewise uncertain in its stem; the -čü is the converb.

morph.gloss: specially, on purpose (form uncertain; Ming 特地 行) [特地 行]
to plot, stir up (stem uncertain; Ming 謀起) [謀起着]

sentences.t: Dalan-Balžud-ta qadquldužu Žeren-e qabčiγaj-a qorγožu
sentences.l: Dalan-Balžud-at fighting-each-other, Žeren-at narrow-place-in hemming-in,
sentences.i: fought at Dalan-Baljut and, at Jeren, in the narrow place, pressed hard —
sentences.n: Both place names carry the Ming 地名行, 'a place, at'. qadquldužu is 'fighting each other' (厮殺着). qorγožu is Ming 敎𧻞着, using a rare character, and I read it as 'hemming in, pressing hard' without being sure.

morph.gloss: to hem in, press hard (Ming 敎𧻞着, a rare character) [敎𧻞着]

sentences.t: nama-ji tende ese-ü ajuγ̇ululaγ̇a či.
sentences.l: Me there not-? frightened you.
sentences.i: did you not frighten me there?
sentences.n: ese-ü: ese 'not' with the interrogative -ü (Ming 不曾麽), a rhetorical question. ajuγ̇ululaγ̇a is aju- 'fear' made causative and put in the past, 'you made (me) afraid'.

sentences.t: Edöġe nököčeje kēġesü ülü boluju.
sentences.l: Now companion-let-us if (you) say, not agreeable.
sentences.i: Now, if you say, ‘Let us be companions,’ it is not agreeable.
sentences.n: kēġesü is keġe- 'say' as a conditional (with the long vowel printed). ülü boluju, Ming 不肯有, is 'not agreeable'. The form boluju differs slightly from bolumui earlier; I do not know the difference.

morph.gloss: to become, be; here 'to be agreeable' (Ming 肯) [肯有]

sentences.t: Amin čin-u qailaγ̇asu ese bolba či keġen ügüledkün.
sentences.l: Life your if (you) had cherished, not become you, saying, speak (pl.).
sentences.i: If you had cherished your life, you would not have come to this: say this.
sentences.n: qailaγ̇asu is the conditional of qaila- 'cherish, spare'. ese bolba či is 'you did not become' (Ming 不曾做了你); I supply 'come to this'. keġen ügüledkün, 'saying, speak', is a command to the listeners to carry the message.

morph.gloss: not (negative of the past tense) [不曾]

sentences.t: Edöġe čin-u üge-ber čisu ülü γarγan nögčiġetügei keġen ügüle"
sentences.l: Now your word-by, blood not bringing-out, let-them-put-to-death, saying, speak!
sentences.i: Now, by your word, let them put you to death without bringing out your blood: say that to him.”
sentences.n: Shiratori closes Chinggis's speech here (ügüle"). üge-ber, 'by the word', is Ming 依着言語, i.e. he grants what Jamuqa asked, a death without shed blood. nögčiġe- is the causative of nögče-: 'cause to pass away'.

morph.gloss: to cause to pass away, put to death [敎過去者︀]

sentences.t: kēġed čisu ülü γarγan nögčiġežü
sentences.l: Having said, blood not bringing-out, having put to death,
sentences.i: Having said this, he ordered, “When you have put him to death without bringing out his blood,
sentences.n: Shiratori prints no opening quotation mark for the order, though he prints the closing one two units on; I supply it in the English, before čisu, and the unit break here is mine. kēġed is keġe- 'say' with the converb -ġed.

morph.gloss: to cause to pass away, put to death [敎過去着]

sentences.t: jasu in-ü ile bu gedkün.
sentences.l: Bone his openly not cast (pl.).
sentences.i: do not cast his bones out in the open.
sentences.n: bu is the prohibitive, with the plural imperative -dkün on ge- (Ming 撇 'cast aside'). ile (Ming 當面) is 'openly, in plain view'. jasu is the short form of jasun 'bone' before in-ü.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to cast aside, throw away (Ming 撇) [撇您]

sentences.t: Saitur baridqun" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Well hold (pl.)”, saying, decree made.
sentences.i: Keep them well!” So he decreed.
sentences.n: baridqun is bari- 'seize, hold' + the plural imperative -dqun (Ming 拿您); 'keep' is the sense in context. keġen žarliγ bolba is the formula for a decree: 'saying, he made a decree'. The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: Žamuqa-ji tende nögčiġežü jasu in-ü bariγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Žamuqa-(object) there having-caused-death, bone his had-held.
sentences.i: There he had Jamuqa put to death, and had his bones taken into keeping.
sentences.n: Žamuqa-ji is the accusative (Ming 行). nögčiġežü and bariγ̇ulba are both causative in form ('caused to die', 'caused to hold'), so the one who gives the order, Chinggis, is the doer; he is unstated, and 'he had … done' is my reading.

morph.gloss: to cause to pass away, put to death [敎過去着]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
